chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Salam ibn Abdullah, from Abu Basir, from Bakr ibn Harb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The decline of the kingdom of So-and-so will not occur until the two swords of So-and-so clash; when they clash, at that time their kingdom will decline.

key_terms.بَنِي فُلَانٍ: Sons of So-and-so (a placeholder for a specific group or family)
key_terms.سَيۡفَا: Two swords (symbolizing two factions or leaders)

ai.seo_question: What is the sign of a kingdom's decline according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) identifies internal division within a ruling dynasty as the definitive sign of its impending collapse, a concept often applied by Shia scholars to the Umayyads or Abbasids. The metaphor of 'two swords clashing' signifies that political fragmentation precedes the actual fall of the kingdom, serving as a key eschatological indicator for the era preceding the Reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.).
